story.title: South Korea's Supreme Court Overturns Conviction of Former Prime Minister Han Duck-so
story.summary: South Korea's Supreme Court has overturned the conviction of former Prime Minister Han Duck-so, who was found guilty of aiding in the legitimization of the 2024 martial law declaration. The case will now be sent back to a lower court for further proceedings.

related_stories.title: Hakeem Jeffries Nominated for House Speaker, Poised to Make History
related_stories.summary: Hakeem Jeffries has been nominated by House Democrats to become the first Black Speaker of the House. In a recent secret ballot, he secured 251 votes in favor and 11 against. His nomination positions him to lead the chamber when Democrats take control in January, although he faces pressure from progressive lawmakers on key issues such as healthcare and immigration.

related_stories.title: European Leaders Reaffirm Support for Ukraine and Push for Peace Talks
related_stories.summary: European leaders convened in Berlin to present a united front in support of Ukraine and to advocate for European involvement in future peace negotiations aimed at ending the ongoing conflict with Russia. The German Chancellor emphasized that any peace talks excluding Europe are likely to fail, reinforcing the need for solidarity with Ukraine.

related_stories.title: International Court of Justice Rules Myanmar Committed Genocide Against Rohingya
related_stories.summary: The International Court of Justice (ICJ) has ruled that Myanmar is guilty of genocide against the Rohingya minority, marking a historic decision as it is the first time a state has been held accountable for genocide by the court. The ruling, passed by a narrow margin of nine votes to six, pertains to the military crackdown in 2017 that resulted in thousands of deaths and widespread displacement of the Rohingya people. The court has called for reparations and the safe return of refugees.
